lesson.title: React useEffect() hook introduction
lesson.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

steps.title: Build the counter component
steps.instructions:
In a new Vite React app (npm create vite@latest, react template), create src/MyComponent.jsx with count state, a

Count: {count}

and an Add button calling addCount (setCount(c => c + 1)), and render it from App.jsx. Run npm run dev.

targets.caption: The count state variable starting at zero
Rendered counter; clicking Add increments it

explanations.topic: Importing useState and useEffect from React
Declaring a state variable with a setter
Updater function using previous state

hints: Start by importing both hooks: import { useState, useEffect } from 'react'.

Declare the state with const [count, setCount] = useState(0) and show it in a

Count: {count}

.
Write function addCount() { setCount(c => c + 1); } and pass it as onClick={addCount} without parentheses.
Make sure App.jsx imports MyComponent and renders <MyComponent />, and that npm run dev is running.
common_mistakes: Writing onClick={addCount()} which calls the function during render and causes an infinite re-render loop.
Forgetting to export default MyComponent or to import/render it in App.jsx.
Returning two sibling elements without wrapping them in a fragment <>...</>.
Importing useEffect from the wrong package or misspelling it (useEffects).

steps.title: Run effect on every render
steps.instructions: Near the top of the component call useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; }) with no second argument. Click Add and watch the tab title update on every re-render.

targets.caption: Effect with no dependency array: runs after every render

explanations.topic: useEffect runs side code every time the component re-renders
useEffect takes two arguments: a function and an array of dependencies
Omitting the second argument means the effect runs on every render
Effect also runs initially when the component mounts

hints: Call useEffect near the top of your component, right after your useState line.
Pass useEffect a single arrow function and leave out the second argument (no dependency array).
Inside the arrow function, assign document.title a template string that includes your count variable.
Don't forget to add useEffect to your import from 'react', then click Add and watch the browser tab title.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import useEffect from 'react' (useEffect is not defined error).
Passing an empty array [] as a second argument, so the title only updates on mount.
Using regular quotes instead of backticks, so ${count} appears literally in the title.
Calling useEffect inside the click handler or conditionally instead of at the top level of the component.
Writing document.title(...) as a function call instead of assigning to it.

steps.title: Run effect only on mount
steps.instructions: Pass an empty dependency array as the second argument, useEffect(() => {...}, []), and confirm the title only updates once on mount (e.g. set it to 'My Counter Program'). Then revert to the count title.

targets.caption: Add an empty array [] as the second argument

explanations.topic: An empty dependency array runs the effect only on mount
Title updates once and not again after pressing add
One-and-done effects: no need to re-run on every re-render
Without [] the effect would run after every re-render

hints: useEffect takes a second argument after the callback function.
Pass an empty array of dependencies so React runs the effect only when the component mounts.
Write it as useEffect(() => { document.title = `My Counter Program`; }, []); then press add and check the tab title doesn't change.
When done, revert the title back to the count version as the presenter does.
common_mistakes: Putting the [] inside the callback body instead of as the second argument to useEffect.
Forgetting the comma between the arrow function and the [] array.
Passing [count] instead of [] so the effect still runs every time count changes.
Expecting the title to change on add clicks after using [], when it now only runs once on mount.
Leaving the 'My Counter Program' title in place instead of reverting to the count title before the next step.

steps.title: Depend on count, add subtract
steps.instructions: Put count in the dependency array ([count]) and add a Subtract button calling subtractCount, which does setCount(c => c - 1), in src/MyComponent.jsx.

explanations.topic: Adding a value to the dependency array runs the effect on mount plus whenever that value changes
With no dependency array the effect runs on every re-render, even for unrelated reasons
With [count] the effect runs only when count updates
The title changes whether count goes up or down: any change to count triggers the effect

hints: Put count inside the empty array that is the second argument to useEffect.
Copy your addCount function, rename it subtractCount, and change + 1 to - 1 using the updater form: setCount(c => c - 1).
Add a <button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button> next to the Add button, then click both buttons and watch the browser tab title.
common_mistakes: Leaving the array empty ([]), so the title only sets on mount and never updates.
Writing onClick={subtractCount()}, which calls the function during render and causes an infinite re-render loop.
Copying addCount but forgetting to change + 1 to - 1, or forgetting to rename the function.
Passing the dependency as a string (['count']) instead of the variable [count].

steps.title: Add color as second dependency
steps.instructions: Add const [color, setColor] = useState('green'), a Change color button calling changeColor that toggles setColor(c => c === 'green' ? 'red' : 'green'), and style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}}. Include color in the title template and add it to the dependency array: [count, color].

explanations.topic: Adding a second piece of state (color) to drive the effect
Updater function using the previous state with a ternary
style attribute needs a JS object, hence double curly braces
Effect doesn't rerun on color change when color isn't a dependency
Dependency array: effect runs whenever any listed value changes

hints: Create another state variable for the color with useState, starting at 'green', and a button whose onClick is a changeColor function.
Inside changeColor, call setColor with an updater: c => c === 'green' ? 'red' : 'green'.
Style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}} — the outer braces embed JS, the inner ones make an object.
Put color in the title template string, then change the dependency array to [count, color] so the title updates when either changes.
common_mistakes: Using single braces style={color: color}, which is a syntax error — style needs an object inside JSX braces.
Writing onClick={changeColor()} which calls the function on every render instead of on click.
Including color in the title but forgetting to add it to the dependency array, so the title doesn't update when only the color changes.
Using = instead of === in the ternary condition, which always assigns 'green'.
Forgetting to import useState/useEffect, or declaring color state after the useEffect that references it in a way that causes a reference error.

steps.title: Track window size with listener
steps.instructions: In a new component, create width/height state initialised to window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight, display 'Window width: {width}px' and 'Window height: {height}px', and write handleResize that sets both. Temporarily call window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize) with console.log('EVENT LISTENER ADDED') directly in the component body and observe listeners piling up in the console.

explanations.topic: State initialised from window.innerWidth / innerHeight
Display doesn't update without a resize listener
addEventListener needs an event name and a callback
Adding a listener in the component body adds a new one on every re-render

hints: You need two useState variables, each initialised from a window property.
handleResize takes no parameters and calls setWidth(window.innerWidth) and setHeight(window.innerHeight).
In the component body, call window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize) followed by console.log("EVENT LISTENER ADDED"), then resize the browser and watch the console count climb.
common_mistakes: Writing setheight instead of setHeight (the presenter corrects this at 13:12).
Passing handleResize() (calling it) instead of handleResize as the callback.
Forgetting the 'px' unit or rendering width twice instead of height.
Not rendering the new component in App.jsx, so nothing appears in the browser.

steps.title: Move listener into mount effect
steps.instructions: Wrap the addEventListener call and the console.log in useEffect(() => {...}, []) so the listener is added only once on mount. Resize the window and confirm the console shows just one add (two in StrictMode).

targets.caption: Wrap addEventListener in a mount effect

explanations.topic: Adding the event listener only once, when the component mounts
An empty dependency array means the effect runs only on mount
StrictMode runs effects twice in development (setup and cleanup cycle)

hints: The listener should be added once, when the component mounts, not on every render.
Move the addEventListener call and its console.log inside useEffect(() => { ... }).
Pass an empty array [] as useEffect's second argument.
If you see the log twice, that's StrictMode in development and is expected.
common_mistakes: Leaving the old top-level addEventListener in the component body, so listeners still pile up on each render
Omitting the dependency array, which makes the effect run after every render
Putting width/height in the dependency array, which re-adds the listener on every resize
Calling handleResize() instead of passing handleResize to addEventListener
Thinking the duplicate log in StrictMode is a bug

steps.title: Return a cleanup function
steps.instructions: Inside the same effect, return () => { window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize); console.log('EVENT LISTENER REMOVED'); }. Refresh and check the console shows the StrictMode add/remove/add cycle.

explanations.topic: Returning a cleanup function from useEffect
Cleanup runs before the next re-render or on unmount
Why to remove listeners: avoid unexpected behavior and free resources
StrictMode add/remove/add cycle in development

hints: The cleanup goes inside the same useEffect that adds the resize listener, as its return value.
Return an arrow function: return () => { ... } just before the closing of the effect callback.
Inside it call window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize) with the exact same handler, then console.log('EVENT LISTENER REMOVED').
Refresh the page and open Inspect > Console; with StrictMode you should see ADDED, REMOVED, ADDED.
common_mistakes: Returning the result of removeEventListener directly (return window.removeEventListener(...)) instead of returning a function, so it runs immediately.
Passing a new inline arrow to removeEventListener instead of the same handleResize reference, so the listener is never removed.
Putting the return in a separate useEffect instead of the one that added the listener.
Typo 'resize' vs 'resized' in the event name so removal silently does nothing.
Expecting REMOVED to appear on every resize; it only appears on StrictMode's dev re-run or unmount with an empty dependency array.

steps.title: Add second effect for title
steps.instructions: Add another hook: useEffect(() => { document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}`; }, [width, height]). Resize the window and watch the tab title track the size.

targets.caption: Second effect sets title from size

explanations.topic: A component can have more than one useEffect hook
Dependency array [width, height] reruns the effect when size changes
Effect runs on mount, so the title is set right away

hints: Add a separate useEffect below the existing one. Don't merge it into the resize-listener effect.
Inside the effect, assign to document.title using a template string (backticks).
Add the dependency array [width, height] so the effect reruns when either size changes.
Full form: useEffect(() => { document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}`; }, [width, height]);
common_mistakes: Using regular quotes instead of backticks, so ${width} appears literally in the title
Omitting the dependency array, so the effect runs on every render
Using an empty array [], so the title never updates after mount
Putting the title code inside the cleanup function of the listener effect
Typing document.Title (wrong case) instead of document.title
